title: Counits in an exact square from normalization on K-injectives
statement:
Let $\mathcal A',\mathcal A,\mathcal B',\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and assume every complex of $\mathcal A'$ and $\mathcal A$ has a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex (a complex receiving only null-homotopic maps from acyclic complexes). Fix additive adjunctions $F':\mathcal B'\rightleftarrows\mathcal A':G'$ and $F:\mathcal B\rightleftarrows\mathcal A:G$, with $F',F$ exact and ordinary counits $\varepsilon'^0,\varepsilon^0$. Let $r:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$ and $s:\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$ be exact additive functors, with $rF'=Fs$, $sG'=Gr$ on objects and morphisms, and with
$$r(\varepsilon'^0_X)=\varepsilon^0_{rX}$$
under these identities for every $X\in\mathcal A'$. Assume $r$ preserves K-injective complexes. Use the canonical termwise derived exact functors $D(-)$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and fixed universal right derived pairs $(RG',\eta')$, $(RG,\eta)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Suppose a natural isomorphism $\beta:D(s)RG'\xrightarrow{\sim}RG D(r)$ is supplied and satisfies only the following normalization, for every K-injective $J$ of $\mathcal A'$:
$$\beta_{QJ}\circ D(s)(\eta'_J)=\eta_{rJ}.$$
There exist derived adjunctions $D(F')\dashv RG'$ and $D(F)\dashv RG$ canonically specified by this Hom formula (and its primed version): for every chain map $f:F(M)\to I$, its derived transpose is
$$\bigl(Q(f)\circ\varphi_M\bigr)^{\sharp_D}=\eta_I\circ Q(f^{\sharp_0}),$$
where $\varphi_M:D(F)(QM)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(FM)$ is the canonical localization comparison and $f^{\sharp_0}$ is the specified ordinary transpose. Their counits satisfy, for every K-injective $I$ and $J$ in the respective source categories,
$$\varepsilon^D_{QI}\circ D(F)(\eta_I)=Q(\varepsilon^0_I),\qquad
\varepsilon'^{D}_{QJ}\circ D(F')(\eta'_J)=Q(\varepsilon'^0_J),$$
and for every $N\in D(\mathcal A')$,
$$D(r)(\varepsilon'^{D}_N)=\varepsilon^D_{D(r)N}\circ D(F)(\beta_N).$$
All equations use the canonical localization and composition comparisons. No assertion that $D(s)RG'$ is a universal right derived pair, and no normalization of $\beta$ on non-K-injective complexes, is assumed.

proof.text: For a supplied quasi-isomorphism q: K → I with I K-injective, put T = Cone(id_K). The inclusion K → T is a monomorphism in each degree, and T is contractible. The map (inclusion,q): K → T ⊕ I is therefore monomorphic. Projection T ⊕ I → I is a homotopy equivalence, so T ⊕ I is K-injective and the two-out-of-three property makes the displayed monomorphism a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the stated arbitrary-resolution hypothesis supplies the monomorphic resolutions used by the K-injective derivability structure. A quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence; any additive functor preserves it. Consequently the K-injective localizer derives the termwise functor followed by Q. Its derived comparison is invertible on K-injectives, and postcomposition of the fixed right-derived pair by any functor remains right derived. These constructions do not identify the independent derived Hom universes.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] for the adjunction on complexes. The exact factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] is an isomorphism, hence directly gives a left-derived pair by Mathlib Functor.isLeftDerivedFunctor_of_inverts. Its postcomposition by RG is still left derived for the same reason. Step 1 gives right-derivedness of RG followed by D(F). Apply Mathlib Adjunction.derived to these four fixed pairs. Its unit factorization, followed by naturality of eta and the formula for the ordinary transpose, proves precisely the displayed Hom formula. Do this for both adjunctions. This is the exact-left specialization of the normalized derived-adjunction construction; no common-universe resolving-class theorem is required.

proof.text: Apply each Hom formula to the ordinary counit. The ordinary triangle identity says its transpose is the identity. Apply the inverse derived Hom equivalence: D(F)(eta_I) followed by the derived counit equals the localization factor followed by Q of the ordinary counit, for every complex I. For any two normalized adjunctions these equations coincide. The right-derived universal property of RG followed by D(F), proved in Step 1, then makes their counits equal. Adjunction.ext_counit makes the adjunctions equal. Repeat for the primed pair.

proof.text: At a K-injective J, eta-prime_J is invertible by Step 1. Precompose the proposed square equality with D(r)D(F-prime)(eta-prime_J), and postcompose with the canonical factor D(r)(QJ) → Q(rJ). For the first side use the primed counit normalization and naturality of the factor for r. For the second side move the square comparison across eta-prime by naturality, move the factor for r across the unprimed counit, combine the three D(F)-images, and apply exactly h-beta at J. Use the unprimed counit normalization (valid on every complex) and naturality of the factor for F. The canonical square comparison is compatible with both termwise factorizations: this follows from mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_hom_app_factors and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac. After these rewrites both composites are Q of the two ordinary-counit arrows; they agree degree by degree by h-epsilon. Cancel the invertible precomposition and postcomposition. The hypothesis that r preserves K-injectives supplies the specialization of the unprimed normalization at rJ.

source.place: Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), with Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); agent exact-square extraction of tower normalization old steps 6-8

proof.text: Write the two square arrows as natural transformations from RG-prime followed by D(F-prime) and D(r) to D(r). Choose a complex representing any derived object N and its supplied K-injective resolution J; localization gives an isomorphism N → QJ. Naturality transports their equality at QJ from Step 4 to equality after postcomposition with D(r) of this isomorphism. Cancel it. Only the given normalization of beta on K-injectives was used.

Both categories are abelian, the target has K-injective resolutions, P is all of K(B) because identity resolutions work and exact F inverts quasi-isomorphisms, and the universe is the common chosen one. The left pair from exact-functor-derived-functor(1) moves from complexes to the homotopy category along the full, object-surjective quotient. Step 2: the counit has transpose 1, so ε^D D(F)(η_I) = Q(ε0_I)φ_{GI}; the φ factor is covered by the statement's comparison convention. Step 3: def-sfb-right-derived-functor states that η is invertible on K-injectives. With essential surjectivity of Q and naturality this fixes the counit and hence the adjunction. Step 5: naturality along u: N ≅ QJ gives the equation for every N. Small cases checked: identity r, s and β, zero categories, unbounded complexes, and β being fixed by its K-injective values. Not a duplicate: lem-kun-derived-adjoint-square-comparison assumes D(W)RR is right derived with normalization on all complexes; lem-sbc-unbounded-exact-adjunction-square is a geometric special case; lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-exact-square-comparison only constructs β.
